pr_title: fix: sum_horizontal should not always cast to int

issue_context.title: `sum_horizontal` on `Duration` returns wrong dtype
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Reproducible example

```python
pl.select(
    pl.sum_horizontal(pl.duration(seconds=10)).alias('sum_duration')
)

shape: (1, 1)
┌──────────────┐
│ sum_duration │
│ ---          │
│ i64          │
╞══════════════╡
│ 10000000     │
└──────────────┘
```


### Log output

_No response_

### Issue description

Sum_horizontal on duration column returns wrong dtype, it returns an int while it should return a `duration `type. This is a regression of how it works because this was correct in 0.18.15.



### Expected behavior

```python
from polars.testing import assert_frame_equal
import datetime
import polars as pl
import polars.selectors as cs

result = pl.select(
    pl.sum_horizontal([pl.duration(seconds=10)]).alias('sum_duration')
)


expected = pl.DataFrame(
    [
        pl.Series("sum_duration", [datetime.timedelta(seconds=10)], dtype=pl.Duration(time_unit='ns')),
    ]
)

assert_frame_equal(expected, result)
```

comments: @ion-elgreco One question is why the time unit of expected series("sum_duration") is `ns` instead of `us`.

> @ion-elgreco I just notice this as the default time uint of `pl.duration` is `us`, IIRC.
> 
> ```python
> def duration(
>     *,
>     .....
>     time_unit: TimeUnit = "us",
> ) -> Expr:
> ```

Ah my bad then the default changed between 0.18.15 and 0.19 :). I created the test on 0.18.15..

Indeed on the newer version it's 'us'. Sorry for the confusion!
